messages:
Maya (sales): Hey team — kickoff for Stargazer POC perf run. They want sustained 250 qps with 99th pct < 250ms for chat completions. Also flagged KMS + SOC2 questions. Can we confirm run plan and blockers?
Alex (solutions): copying previous runbook but short version: steady ramp to 250qps over 15m, 1h steady, 10m cool-down. Mixed prompt sizes: 40% short (50 tokens), 40% med (200 tokens), 20% long (600 tokens).
Rita (perf-eng): That mix looks fine. We'll run on ded-dev cluster w/ 4xA10s, model = redwood-3b-quant. Need to know if customer requires private VPC or we can use dedicated in our cloud.
Tom (Stargazer): We prefer dedicated (reserved) capacity in us-west and KMS for key wrap. Also can we simulate 2% burst spikes to 1k qps for 30s?
Rita (perf-eng): Yes can add poisson bursts. For 1k qps spikes we'll add two bursts during the 1h steady window. Expect tail jitter — will record p50/p95/p99 and p99.9.
Dan (sre): FYI: if bursts overlap scale-up, autoscaling cooldowns might still trigger throttling. Recommend pre-warming by 10% headroom (i.e., size cluster for 275qps).
Alex (solutions): Noted. Maya, pricing ask: customer wants estimate for sustained 250 qps + 2 spikes/day for 30m. Roughly estimate unit cost?
Maya (sales): Throw us a ballpark so Tom can check budget. Also they asked about SLA for Dedicated.
Rita (perf-eng): Ballpark compute cost: with caching & batching tuned, per-token compute ~ $0.0025 for that model under this mix. For their request assume 500 tokens/session avg => 0.0025 * 500 = $1.25 per session. Multiply by sessions/sec => rough monthly. I'll send detailed calc after run.
Priya (security): Quick note — Stargazer sent our security questionnaire: they require customer-managed KMS and encrypted at rest/in-transit, plus audit logs retention 1 year. Can Dedicated support customer KMS?
Alex (solutions): Dedicated supports BYOK via our KMS integration; for Private (VPC) we can also support HSM in some regions. Audit log retention configurable via Console (we can export logs to their S3).
Tom (Stargazer): Good. Can you share the run schedule? We prefer tomorrow 10:00 PT.
Rita (perf-eng): We can do tomorrow 10:00 PT. Plan: 10:00 ramp (15m), 10:15 steady (1h), bursts at 10:30 and 10:50. We'll post results + perf artifacts.
BenchBot: [automated] Bench job created: job_id=jb_2024_08_stargazer_001. Logs will be uploaded to /bench/2024/08/1777777777/.
Maya (sales): Tom — we'll need a short token to call API (scoped) and allowed IPs for dedicated egress. Can you send?
Tom (Stargazer): Sending IPs + limited API key to alex@stargazer.com now.
Alex (solutions): Received. Setting up test credentials. ETA ~20m.
Rita (perf-eng): Quick sanity check — can you confirm prompt distribution list (send sample prompts)? We need to craft realistic latency-sensitive prefix cache cases.
Tom (Stargazer): Sent sample prompts to Alex; includes doc-summary style and multi-turn chat.
Rita (perf-eng): Got them. Also enabling prefix caching for repeated 1st-turn prompts. That will reduce cost on med prompts.
Dan (sre): One more ops note: if they require KMS key in their account, latency to KMS could add ~5-15ms per session for key unwrap. We'll measure with KMS on/off during run.
Priya (security): Also confirm SOC2 controls: we can provide SOC2 attestation for Dedicated; legal will attach cert.
Maya (sales): Thanks — final preflight checklist: credentials (done), IP allowlist (done), model pinned (redwood-3b-quant), runbook (Rita), run time (tomorrow 10PT), KMS scenario toggles (Dan), pricing ballpark (Rita to finalize). Anything else?
Tom (Stargazer): One ask: Can you include p99.9 and tail covg plots and raw latency CSV? We need those for our SRE review.
Rita (perf-eng): We'll include: p50/p95/p99/p99.9, qps/time, error rate, cold-start vs steady histograms, and link to raw CSV. Also annotate when bursts happen.
BenchBot: [automated] Reminder scheduled: run starting in 23h 12m.
Alex (solutions): I'll draft a short runbook snippet for their ops: how to swap in private KMS, and how to interpret the heatmaps.
Maya (sales): Great. Tom — once run completes we'll follow up with cost model and suggested quantization/ batching tweaks to hit their 99th SLA.
Tom (Stargazer): Appreciate it. One more security Q: can logs be redacted? We need PII redaction.
Priya (security): We support configurable PII redaction at ingestion via redaction policy; will need sample PII patterns. Priya to share redaction guide post-run.
Rita (perf-eng): FYI: if redaction runs pre-inference it'll slightly increase latency (measured ~8-12ms). We'll measure with redaction flag on/off.
Maya (sales): OK team — let's proceed. Post mortem: capture any SLA failures and suggested mitigations.
Alex (solutions): Noted. I'll sync with Rita after run for slides.
BenchBot: [automated] run_complete: jb_2024_08_stargazer_001 status=COMPLETED. Artifacts: /bench/2024/08/1777777777/results.zip
Rita (perf-eng): Quick summary from completed run: steady 250 qps achieved, p99 = 210ms, p99.9 = 340ms (spike windows). Error rate 0.03% (retries due to transient kernel OOMs during spikes). Uploading artifacts now.
Maya (sales): Tom — initial result looks close to target; p99 under 250ms but p99.9 over during bursts. We'll propose pre-warm + slight headroom in Dedicated sizing to cover p99.9.
Tom (Stargazer): Thanks — can you send the cost delta for pre-warming 10%? Also any config changes to reduce p99.9?
Rita (perf-eng): Pre-warm 10% adds ~$1.9k/month for their projected usage. To reduce p99.9: increase batching window slightly, enable KV prefix cache for first-turns, and pin fewer quantization layers (trade quality at tail). I'll include a run with those toggles next week.
Dan (sre): Ops item: we should run the same test with customer KMS in their account to measure unwrap latency.
Maya (sales): I'll schedule follow-up tests and pricing update. Thanks all :tada:
Tom (Stargazer): Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Priya (security): Will share redaction guide and SOC2 attestation later today.
Rita (perf-eng): Uploaded results link: https://storage.redwood.ai/bench/2024/08/1777777777/results.zip (contains raw CSVs, heatmaps, run parameters).
Maya (sales): Closing thread — follow-ups scheduled.
